Columns of the Where To Work dataprep.csv template

Source: R/dataprep.R
dataprep_columns.Rd

The columns of a Where To Work (WTW) project's dataprep.csv template, with their descriptions: the default columns of create_dataprep_template(). They are the columns wtw-data-prep2's step 01 writes, with its descriptions, which the template's second row holds.

Usage

dataprep_columns()

Value

A named character vector of eight elements: the names are the columns, in the template's order, and the values their descriptions:

  • conversion_ready_input: "full filepath to input data";

  • short_name: "10 characters or less name for variable";

  • tif_output: "full filepath with extension to output tif";

  • unit: "supported units: m2, ha, km2, m, km and count";

  • stat: "supported stats: mean, max, min, sum, stdev, mode and area ";

  • cell_value: "if stat is area, provide cell value to extract";

  • datatype: "supported types: raster, vector";

  • provenance: "national or regional".

Method

No computation: the columns and descriptions are wtw-data-prep2's, as its create_project_folder() writes them, character for character (including the space at the end of the stat description). The ArcGIS toolbox of wtw-data-prep2 (wtw-utils) reads conversion_ready_input, short_name, tif_output, unit, stat, cell_value and datatype; provenance is for documentation. The toolbox's own checks, and the wtw-data-prep2 manual, say which values each column takes; the descriptions here are the template's text, not those rules.

See also

create_dataprep_template(), which writes the template.

Other wtw: create_dataprep_template(), create_wtw_planning_units(), create_wtw_project_folder(), extract_wtw_natdata(), wtw_project_folders()

Examples

dataprep_columns()
#>                                        conversion_ready_input 
#>                                 "full filepath to input data" 
#>                                                    short_name 
#>                     "10 characters or less name for variable" 
#>                                                    tif_output 
#>                  "full filepath with extension to output tif" 
#>                                                          unit 
#>               "supported units: m2, ha, km2, m, km and count" 
#>                                                          stat 
#> "supported stats: mean, max, min, sum, stdev, mode and area " 
#>                                                    cell_value 
#>              "if stat is area, provide cell value to extract" 
#>                                                      datatype 
#>                             "supported types: raster, vector" 
#>                                                    provenance 
#>                                        "national or regional" 

# The column names only
names(dataprep_columns())
#> [1] "conversion_ready_input" "short_name"             "tif_output"            
#> [4] "unit"                   "stat"                   "cell_value"            
#> [7] "datatype"               "provenance"
